newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile insists on more details on Russia probe.
newsitem.headline: Chile insists on more details on Russia probe.

text.p: Chile insisted on Tuesday that it needs more information from Russian scientists to find the wreck of the Mars 96 space probe that U.S. space experts said may have crashed to Earth in the northern Atacama Desert.
Russian authorities have said the satellite, carrying radioactive plutonium, plunged into the Pacific Ocean hundreds of miles (kilometres) further west between Easter Island and Chile's mainland.

"We agree that the object re-entered the atmosphere on Nov. 16 but there are important disagreements as to where it fell," Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza told reporters. "The problem is the Russians have repeated their previous information ... but have not given any new details which would allow us to carry out a more precise search."

Although most of the probe was thought to have burned out on re-entry, the U.S. space agency NASA last week said a part of the craft may have fallen in a large area of land and sea in northern Chile. The report sparked searches by the Chilean air force and navy for traces of radiation from the satellite, which was carrying eight ounces (200 grams) of plutonium.

Russian officials rejected remarks by Chilean Defence Minister Edmundo Perez on Monday that Russia was unwilling to hand over information to help in the hunt for the wreck. "Our instructions have always been to hand over all the information we have to Chilean state bodies," embassy counsellor Vladimir Troukjanobski told evening newspaper La Segunda.
Although the tests have not shown any contamination, there have been reports of witnesses seeing the spacecraft burn up in the atmosphere near the northern port of Antofagasta.
Russian scientists have said there is no danger of radioactive pollution as the plutonium is stored in containers designed to withstand the heat and stress of landing on Mars.
The Mars 96 satellite fell back to Earth after takeoff when a booster rocket misfired, preventing the craft from breaking free of Earth's gravity.
